title: prefill-unexpected-latency-sleuth-brief-jun-2026
content:
Purpose:
Quick investigation notes from this week on a recurring, low-volume latency spike that appears correlated with prefill shadowing + small-batch routing. This is an informal lab-style write-up intended to capture hypotheses, quick experiments, and next steps before we fold into a formal postmortem.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Observed short (~200–600ms) p95 spikes for tail requests on two clusters between 2026-06-03 and 2026-06-06.
- Spikes coincide with prefill shadow flows and a rise in 1–2 token KV cache misses in late-stage microbatches.
- Root cause appears to be an interaction between the prefill shadow path and our early-exit kernel handshake logic that forces synchronous KV loads for some tiny batches.
- Short-term mitigation applied (fallback to soft-prefill for shadow traffic) brought incidents to zero for 36 hours on canary nodes.

Metrics snapshot (observed):
- Normal p50: 18–22ms (token gen path)
- Normal p95: 42–55ms
- Spike p95 observed: 260–610ms (durations measured at request ingress)
- Affected percentile: p97–p99.9, ~0.03% of requests in window
- KV cache hit-rate drop from 98.6% -> 92.1% on affected hosts
- Average batch size for affected requests: 1.2 tokens per microbatch (heavy singletons)

What we saw (chronology):
- Wed 2026-06-02: Nightly synthetic prefill job updated to include a new shadowing flag (shadow_prefill=true) to exercise competing prefill paths (INF-846).
- Thu 2026-06-03 09:20 UTC: Pager triggered for elevated p95 on cluster asia-west-2-prefill-3. Slack thread: #serving-runtime-ops (see linked_artifacts).
- Thu 2026-06-03 10:05 UTC: SRE rolled back the shadowing flag for the nightly job. Short-term improvement but not full resolution.
- Fri 2026-06-04: Engineers repro'd locally with reduced load and traced a ~400ms synchronous disk read in the kernel handshake on singleton-batched requests.

Hypotheses we considered:
1) Disk-backed KV eviction (hot reload) caused synchronous reads on tiny batches. (Partially supported by increased disk IO on the host.)
2) Kernel handshake path for early-exit batches is incorrectly bypassing async-prefetch and waiting on KV readiness. (Strongly supported by traces.)
3) Shadow prefill flow races with cache warmup and inserts explicit backpressure into the sampler, causing delays for subsequent singleton microbatches. (Weakly supported; timing lines up but instrumentation needed.)

Experiments run (quick log):
- EXP-A (2026-06-04 14:00 UTC) - Toggle early-exit handshake flag to opt into async-prefetch path. Result: p95 improved by ~70% for the repro scenario.
- EXP-B (2026-06-04 16:30 UTC) - Throttle shadow-prefill to randomized 5% sampling. Result: partial reduction in KV miss storms; tail still present but lower frequency.
- EXP-C (2026-06-05 02:10 UTC) - Force immediate KV insert after shadow prefill (no lock). Result: race reduced locally but revealed an ordering bug (double-insert) in shadow pipeline.

Root cause (working theory):
- A combination of the early-exit handshake optimization (to short-circuit long sequences) and the new prefill shadow routine led to a rare codepath where a microbatch with 1 token was routed through a synchronous kernel handshake that performed blocking KV lookups. When shadowing is enabled, the timing occasionally causes the cache entry to be absent, triggering disk-backed loads that we treat synchronously in that handshake. The interplay produces 200–600ms tail latency.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Reverted the nightly shadow_prefill=true on all synthetic jobs (SRE).
- Deployed handshake flag defaulting to async-prefetch on canary pool (serving-runtime v2.18.3-hotfix).
- Added a short-term sampler guard: if microbatch.size <= 2, prefer fast-path routing that avoids blocking KV syncs.

Longer-term proposals / options (tradeoffs listed):
1) Change handshake to always return immediately and drive KV loads in the background with promise/future reconciliation. Pros: eliminates blocking read tail; Cons: more complex correctness surface and potential for stale reads if not reconciled carefully.
2) Introduce a small in-memory prefetch buffer for entries touched by prefill shadow to reduce disk misses. Pros: cheap and localized; Cons: memory pressure and additional invalidation complexity.
3) Rework shadow prefill to back off insertion order and to use duplicate-suppressing writes. Pros: addresses the race; Cons: requires changes across prefill pipeline and verification.

Decisions made this week:
- Short term: Keep handshake async-prefetch default on canary and roll to stable once we have full e2e tests.
- Medium term: Implement option #3 (duplicate-suppressing writes in shadow prefill) with a safety QA window. Owner: Jules Park. ETA: 2026-06-21.
- Investigate option #1 as a follow-up spike (spike owner: Victor Alvarez). Deliverable: prototype async handshake with correctness tests by 2026-07-02.

Open questions / unknowns:
- What percentage of customer traffic uses microbatch sizes of 1–2 tokens? (Data: partial, need product telemetry team to add per-route microbatch histogram)
- Are there other codepaths that still perform synchronous disk reads during kernel handshake? (Action: full trace sweep across stable kernels; owner: Ethan Chen)
- What is the memory cost of an in-memory prefetch buffer at cluster scale? (Action: capacity model; owner: Mariana Gomez)

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Jules Park: Implement duplicate-suppressing writes for shadow prefill, PR + integration tests. Due: 2026-06-18.
- Ethan Chen: Run full kernel handshake trace sweep and list synchronous disk read sites; document findings. Due: 2026-06-14.
- Mariana Gomez: Capacity model for in-memory prefetch buffer (cluster-wide memory delta). Due: 2026-06-17.
- Aisha Patel (me): Draft formal postmortem and change proposal for service review. Due: 2026-06-22.
- SRE (oncall): Keep shadow_prefill disabled in nightly jobs until PR lands. Status: done.

Meeting notes (standup on 2026-06-05):
Attendees: Aisha, Ethan, Jules, Mariana, Victor, Grace (SRE).
- Quick sync: reproduce confirmed locally, root cause narrowed to handshake + shadow ordering.
- Safety decision: avoid wide rollout of shadow prefill until duplicate-suppressing writes exist.
- Risk table: show small risk of increased memory if we add prefetch buffer; prefer code fix first.

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Re-check the eviction policy for tiny entries (TTL vs LRU); TTL R/W path might be doing a disk compaction that we overlooked.
- Add a small end-to-end test that simulates: shadow prefill -> immediate read from another request -> ensure no synchronous disk read is triggered.
- Consider adding a sampler metric: "shadow-insert-latency" to catch micro-race sooner.

Related tickets/PRs (quick list):
- INF-846 (latency repro and investigation)
- INF-859 (shadow prefill duplicate suppression) - planned
- PR #2146 (handshake async-prefetch toggle) - landed on canary

Appendix (traces & snippets):
- Trace example (stack): kernel::handshake() -> kv::lookup_blocking() -> disk::sync_read() -> wait -> kernel::resume()
- Quick patch note: handshake_async_prefetch=false previously caused 3x higher tail in local repro.

If you have follow-ups, paste into the slack thread or add comments here. Planning to fold this into a formal postmortem once Jules' PR lands and we have one week of stable canary telemetry.

-- Aisha
